title: A fail-fast ring buffer you can loop over

task.text: A log viewer keeps the latest lines in a ring buffer. Make it `Iterable` without exposing its array.
Finish `RingBuffer<T>` in `RingBuffer.java`; the constructor and `size()` are done.

items: `add(T)` appends. When the buffer is full it overwrites the oldest element.
`iterator()` walks from the oldest element to the newest, so `for (T x : buffer)` works.
Every call returns an independent cursor; `hasNext()` never advances it.
`next()` past the end throws `NoSuchElementException`; `remove()` is unsupported.
The cursor is fail-fast: if the buffer was changed by `add` after the cursor was created, `next()` throws `ConcurrentModificationException`.

checks.title: A full buffer overwrites the oldest element
Running out of elements raises NoSuchElementException
hasNext() does not move the cursor
A new cursor sees the changed buffer
The buffer hands out separate cursor objects

hints.text: Traversal state (how far you are) does not belong in the collection. Put it in a small cursor object that the buffer creates on every `iterator()` call.
Return an anonymous `Iterator<T>` that remembers `modCount` when created and keeps its own `offset`. The element at `offset` lives at slot `(start + offset) % slots.length`.

lines: public boolean hasNext() { return offset < size; }
